key_insight: RLQ-Grad uses a reinforcement-learning policy to propose QNN parameter updates, avoiding backpropagation through the quantum circuit and thereby sidestepping barren-plateau gradient collapse and exponential differentiation cost.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical training alternative for near-term quantum hardware, with much lower memory/time overhead and better scalability as qubit counts grow.
method: Spectrally normalized PPO actor-critic learns update steps from current parameters, loss, accuracy, and previous update.
The surrogate gradient is generated by a classical policy network instead of differentiating through the unitary circuit.
Training cost scales with trainable parameters rather than the Hilbert-space dimension.
evidence_signal: Across four supervised benchmarks up to 20 qubits, RLQ-Grad kept gradient variance nearly flat, used under 2 MB memory, and was reported to run 2490×, 7876×, and 673× faster per iteration than backpropagation, parameter-shift, and adjoint differentiation, respectively.
watch_item: Because the method depends on RL rollouts and actor-critic training, its stability and sample efficiency may be sensitive to reward design, policy tuning, and benchmark transferability.
paper_title: Modeling quantum neural network gradient with reinforcement learning
